title: How do you mark positive and negative numbers on a line?
description: Three positive and three negative numbers are marked on the number line from negative ten to ten. Counting steps right of zero gives the positive marks and steps left of zero gives the negative marks, and the places are checked at the end.
teaching_notes: One idea: count steps from zero, right for a positive number and left for a negative number. Watch for students who place a bigger negative number nearer to zero.

video_script.why: The child marks three positive numbers to the right of zero and three negative numbers to the left of zero on the book's number line, by counting steps from zero.
video_script.substitution: The book's own number line from negative ten to ten, with one choice of three positive and three negative numbers.
video_script.anchor: the number line of the book from negative ten to ten
video_script.payoff_line: Any three marks to the right of zero and any three to the left will work.

final_answer.value: Open-ended. Example: A = 2, B = 5, C = 8; P = -1, Q = -3, R = -7
final_answer.spoken: any three positive and three negative numbers work, for example two, five, eight, and negative one, negative three, negative seven

maths_rules: walk from 0: n steps right marks the positive number n
n steps left marks the negative number -n
choice made here: A = 2, B = 5, C = 8 to the right of 0; P = -1, Q = -3, R = -7 to the left of 0
check: -7 < -3 < -1 < 0 < 2 < 5 < 8, each smaller number lies to the left of the bigger one
any three positive and any three negative numbers between -10 and 10 would also be right
